title: Hyponatraemia (adult)
subject: nephrology
summary: Treat severe symptoms with 150 mL 3% saline boluses aiming for a 5 mmol/L rise, classify by osmolality and volume status, then correct by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours (8 mmol/L in high ODS risk) and re-lower promptly if overcorrected.

sections.title: Recognise and classify
items: Hyponatraemia: serum sodium below 135 mmol/L. Mild 130 to 135, moderate 125 to 129, profound below 125 mmol/L (ESE 2014). Acute if documented within 48 hours, otherwise treat as chronic.
Severe symptoms: vomiting, cardiorespiratory distress, abnormal deep somnolence, seizures, coma (GCS 8 or less). Moderately severe: nausea without vomiting, confusion, headache.
Confirm hypotonicity: measured serum osmolality below 275 mOsm/kg. Exclude hyperglycaemia, mannitol and pseudohyponatraemia (severe hyperlipidaemia or paraproteinaemia).
Urine osmolality 100 mOsm/kg or less: excess water intake or low solute intake (beer potomania, tea and toast diet).
Urine osmolality above 100 and urine sodium 30 mmol/L or less: low effective arterial volume (GI losses, heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome).

Urine sodium above 30 mmol/L: diuretics (especially thiazides), kidney disease, SIAD, adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, cerebral or renal salt wasting. Assess ECF volume clinically to separate these.

sections.title: Severe symptoms: first hour
items: Give 150 mL 3% sodium chloride IV over 20 minutes; check sodium at 20 minutes while giving a second 150 mL over the next 20 minutes. Repeat up to two times (three boluses) or until sodium has risen by 5 mmol/L.
Consider 2 mL/kg of 3% saline instead of 150 mL when body size is markedly abnormal.

Once sodium has risen 5 mmol/L and symptoms improve: stop hypertonic saline, keep the line open with minimal 0.9% saline, start cause-specific treatment, and check sodium at 6 and 12 hours, then daily.

If symptoms do not improve after a 5 mmol/L rise: continue 3% saline aiming for about 1 mmol/L/h further rise; stop when symptoms improve, sodium has risen 10 mmol/L in total, or reaches 130 mmol/L. Check sodium every 4 hours.
Moderately severe symptoms: a single 150 mL 3% saline infusion over 20 minutes, aiming for a 5 mmol/L rise per 24 hours; check sodium at 1, 6 and 12 hours.
Acute fall of more than 10 mmol/L without severe symptoms: a single 150 mL 3% saline infusion over 20 minutes and recheck sodium after 4 hours.

sections.title: Correction limits and chronic hyponatraemia
items: Limit the rise to 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours and 8 mmol/L in every 24 hours thereafter until sodium reaches 130 mmol/L (ESE 2014).
High ODS risk (sodium 105 mmol/L or less, hypokalaemia, alcohol use disorder, malnutrition, advanced liver disease): do not exceed 8 mmol/L in any 24 hours (US expert panel 2013).

Chronic without moderate or severe symptoms: stop non-essential fluids and culprit drugs (thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine, PPIs), treat the cause, and do not give treatment solely to raise sodium in mild hyponatraemia.
Hypovolaemic: restore ECF volume with 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid at 0.5 to 1.0 mL/kg/h; expect a brisk water diuresis once volume is restored.
Hypervolaemic (heart failure, cirrhosis): fluid restriction and treatment of the underlying condition; avoid hypertonic saline unless symptoms are severe.
Correcting hypokalaemia also raises serum sodium; include potassium given in the correction estimate.

sections.title: SIAD
items: First line: fluid restriction, for example about 500 mL/day below the 24-hour urine volume (US panel). Likely to fail if urine osmolality is above 500 mOsm/kg or urine sodium plus potassium exceeds serum sodium.
Second line (ESE): oral urea 0.25 to 0.50 g/kg/day, or low-dose loop diuretic with oral sodium chloride.

Vaptans: ESE advises against them in moderate or profound hyponatraemia because of overcorrection risk; the US panel lists tolvaptan as an option, started in hospital with close sodium monitoring and no fluid restriction in the first 24 hours.
ESE recommends against lithium and demeclocycline.

Look for the cause: pneumonia, TB, CNS disease, malignancy (small cell lung cancer), pain, nausea, postoperative state and drugs; exclude hypothyroidism and adrenal insufficiency before labelling SIAD.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Serum sodium at the intervals above during active treatment, plus hourly urine output and fluid balance.
A sudden rise in urine output (dilute water diuresis) after volume repletion, cortisol replacement, or stopping a culprit drug predicts rapid overcorrection: recheck sodium within 2 hours.
Check potassium, glucose and volume status alongside sodium.

sections.title: Overcorrection rescue
items: If sodium rises more than 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours or more than 8 mmol/L in any later 24 hours: stop active treatment and seek expert advice.
Re-lower sodium with electrolyte-free water (5% dextrose) 10 mL/kg IV over 1 hour, under strict urine output and fluid balance monitoring.
Add desmopressin 2 mcg IV, not repeated more often than every 8 hours (expert advice).
Severe symptoms, seizures, or sodium below 120 mmol/L with high ODS risk: manage in HDU or ICU.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Using 0.9% saline in SIAD: it can lower sodium further when urine osmolality is high.
Missing adrenal insufficiency or hypothyroidism as the cause of euvolaemic hyponatraemia.
Delaying 3% saline in severe symptoms for fear of ODS; the risk is from exceeding daily limits, not from the first 5 mmol/L.
Not anticipating the water diuresis that follows correction of hypovolaemia or stopping thiazides.

drugs.name: Sodium chloride 3% (hypertonic saline)
drugs.dose: 150 mL IV over 20 minutes, repeated up to twice (three doses) until sodium rises 5 mmol/L
drugs.notes: Severe symptoms. Consider 2 mL/kg with abnormal body size. A single 150 mL dose for moderately severe symptoms.

drugs.name: Tolvaptan
drugs.dose: 15 mg orally once daily, titrated to 30 to 60 mg by sodium response
drugs.notes: US panel option, not ESE. Start in hospital, no fluid restriction for the first 24 hours; avoid in liver disease; not beyond 30 days.

drugs.name: Glucose 5% (electrolyte-free water)
drugs.notes: To re-lower sodium after overcorrection, with expert advice.

drugs.name: Desmopressin
drugs.dose: 2 mcg IV, not more often than every 8 hours
